<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-olive-oil" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-olive-oil-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of olive oil, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤5</td><td>≤10</td><td>≤20</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤5</td><td>≤10</td><td>≤20</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>55 reference units; 5 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>48</td><td>20%</td></tr><tr><td>FDA Total Diet Study</td><td>3</td><td>20%</td></tr><tr><td>Ashraf 2012</td><td>1</td><td>20%</td></tr><tr><td>Sallam et al. 2025</td><td>2</td><td>20%</td></tr><tr><td>Spungen et al. 2024</td><td>1</td><td>20%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for olive oil, oil on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>5 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" data-no-cite-meta>FDA Total Diet Study</a></li><li><a href="../sources/ashraf2012-heavy-metals-vegetable-oils-saudi-arabia" class="internal" data-slug="sources/ashraf2012-heavy-metals-vegetable-oils-saudi-arabia" data-no-cite-meta>Ashraf 2012</a></li><li><a href="../sources/sallam2025-olive-oil-libya-traditional-modern" class="internal" data-slug="sources/sallam2025-olive-oil-libya-traditional-modern" data-no-cite-meta>Sallam et al. 2025</a></li><li><a href="../sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium" class="internal" data-slug="sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium" data-no-cite-meta>Spungen et al. 2024</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach olive Oil

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach olive Oil comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Olive Oil, oil from refined had nickel higher at 14.1 µg/kg, against 0.721 µg/kg for unrefined in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lin S-T, Liao K-W, Xuan T-C, Chiou T-Y, Lin Z-E, Lee W-J · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-olive-oil" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-olive-oil" data-question="How do heavy metals get into olive Oil?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into olive Oil?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, olive Oil from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than olive Oil from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lin S-T, Liao K-W, Xuan T-C, Chiou T-Y, Lin Z-E, Lee W-J · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Determination, distribution, and health risk assessment of 12 heavy metals in various edible oils in Taiwan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">JSFA Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Olive Oil, oil from refined had lead higher at 3.34 µg/kg, against 1.52 µg/kg for unrefined in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lin S-T, Liao K-W, Xuan T-C, Chiou T-Y, Lin Z-E, Lee W-J · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Determination, distribution, and health risk assessment of 12 heavy metals in various edible oils in Taiwan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">JSFA Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-olive-oil-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-olive-oil-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of olive Oil measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of olive Oil measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 15 groups of olive Oil ranged from 150 µg/kg (harvested from the ground; sample Kal10) to 1,480 µg/kg (harvested directly from the plantation tree; sample Kal7); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/luka2019-northern-cyprus-olive-oil-metals|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Moses Farrell Luka, Ertan Akun · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/luka2019-northern-cyprus-olive-oil-metals">Investigation of trace metals in different varieties of olive oils from northern Cyprus and their variation in accumulation using ICP-MS and multivariate techniques</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Earth Sciences</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/luka2019-northern-cyprus-olive-oil-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 9 groups of olive Oil ranged from 10 µg/kg (glass bottle, 2021/2022 campaign (sample EVOO-P1)) to 100 µg/kg (porcelain (ceramic) container, 2021/2022 campaign (sample EVPR1)); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/charfi2026-olive-oil-packaging-heavy-metals-phthalates|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Charfi A, Moya López AJ, Sánchez Villasclaras S · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/charfi2026-olive-oil-packaging-heavy-metals-phthalates">Food safety in the production of olive oils. Presence of heavy metals and phthalic acid esters using different types of packaging</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/charfi2026-olive-oil-packaging-heavy-metals-phthalates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-olive-oil-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-olive-oil-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in olive Oil is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in olive Oil is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 10 results from 4 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bodur2023-olive-oil-inorganic-arsenic-speciation|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Suleyman Bodur, Sezin Erarpat, Omer Faruk Tutar, Sezgin Bakirdere · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bodur2023-olive-oil-inorganic-arsenic-speciation">Spray assisted preconcentration method combined with HPLC - Continuous flow hydride generation - FAAS for inorganic arsenic speciation in olive oil samples</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Composition and Analysis</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bodur2023-olive-oil-inorganic-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals|17]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Marín S, Pardo O, Sánchez A, Sanchis Y, Vélez D, Devesa V, Font G, Yusà V · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals">Assessment of metal levels in foodstuffs from the Region of Valencia
